output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show that, from 4 Oct, the line system sent a 36-month shelf life to the printers. Nobody overrode it, and the printers printed what they were sent. Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol on 3 Oct. It is only meant to apply to lots made from March 2027, and the 24-month value is still the one in effect. The line system evidently used the future-dated value anyway, which contradicts the vendor's statement. That also explains why two Line 1 day-shift jobs by permanent staff were wrong. Jobs before 4 Oct, including those after the firmware change, were correct. The camera only checks print against the job, so it passed every carton.

I'm fairly confident in this. Still unknown: why the line system read the future value, and whether other products are affected.

Next steps:
- Do not warn or remove the agency operators.
- Fix the Veltranol shelf-life records.
- Extend the hold to every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse.
- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
- Check the two other products with future-dated edits.
- Ask the vendor and IT why the future value was read.
- Keep the camera check switched on.
